problem: "Staging is a copy of production" is too absolute; real staging differs in data volumes, credentials and sometimes hostnames, so a student may believe exact equality is required and be confused when staging reveals differences at release time.
fix: Staging mirrors production as closely as possible: same operating system, configuration and deployment method, but with sanitised or scaled-down data. It is the rehearsal ground, not a byte-for-byte clone.

problem: The chapter says a version number "has three parts" and then uses 2.5.0-rc1, which carries a fourth element. A student may wonder whether the RC tag is part of the version or not.
fix: A release version has three parts, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. A pre-release identifier may be appended with a hyphen, as in 2.5.0-rc1; it marks the build as a candidate and is dropped, unchanged, at final release.
